issues.on_page: Gain (Loss) on Disposal of Capital Assets 118,258 (nonoperating revenues, Total enterprise column)
issues.issue: This is a net gain on disposal, not sale proceeds. Lincoln_FY2024 recorded the same row (a loss that year) as category 'Loss on Disposal of Assets'. A matching 'Gain on Disposal of Assets' category, or confirming Sale of Property, is a judgment call.
Category 'other' while the printed label is not other/miscellaneous. The page gives no nature, so no specific category clearly fits. Already flagged for review. The same applies to detail[8].

issues.on_page: Administrative Costs 64,058,789 (operating expenses listed by cost type)
issues.issue: The utility cost-type rule gives cost-type rows a cost category plus function 'utilities'. This row is a cost type but is categorized as the function 'utilities' with no function field. It matches Lincoln_FY2024, so it is consistent, but it is questionable under the rule.
The extractor's assumption: the page does not state that this is highway allocation (review note present).

Lincoln ruling: Interest is its own category, and 'Principal Retirement' rows are Bond Retirement. The COPs rows (detail[152] COPs Principal 2,675,000, detail[153] COPs Interest) use generic Debt Service instead. This is defensible because they are certificates of participation, not bonds, but check consistency with the Lincoln ruling. Lincoln_FY2024 has no COPs rows to compare.
Interest charged on special assessments. Special assessments is defensible, but the user's Interest Income / Penalties and Interest rulings could also apply.
Label mismatch: the sibling rows use 'Restricted for: ...'. Same for equity[5].

issues.extracted: nonmajor special revenue funds, one line per fund column (17 funds, pp16-17)
issues.on_page: 17 fund columns plus a Total column
issues.issue: Cross-year inconsistency. Lincoln_FY2024 recorded nonmajor special revenue from the Total column as 'Nonmajor funds (combined)'. FY2023 follows the per-fund rule (Total column never used), so FY2023 is correct and FY2024 is the outlier.
